grade.first_issue: No decisive defect; none of Rules A–F imposes a cap.
grade.summary: The proof is complete and correct. The lexicographically decreasing potential establishes finite termination and the positivity of the total prime-factor count ensures that exactly one entry greater than 1 remains. Primewise gcds of the valuation vectors are correctly shown to be invariant, and at a terminal board they determine every exponent of the unique remaining integer, proving independence of all choices.
strengths: The change in the total number of prime factors is computed correctly.
The two cases gcd(m,n)>1 and gcd(m,n)=1 give a valid well-founded lexicographic descent.
The argument rules out a terminal board consisting entirely of 1s.
The valuation transformation and preservation of the gcd of all valuation coordinates are correct, including zero coordinates.
The terminal valuation reconstruction uniquely determines M from the initial board.
